label: Bible Study
prompt: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put _____.
verse: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
note: Jesus on marriage, right after quoting Genesis 2 — what God joins, people shouldn't pull apart.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: How goodly are thy _____, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!
verse: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!
note: Hired to curse Israel, Balaam looks down at their camp and blesses it instead: how goodly are thy tents!

label: Sunday School
prompt: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a _____ a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
verse: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
note: The KJV's 'penny' was a denarius, a day's wage — and in this parable the latecomers got paid the very same.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a _____ beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
verse: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
note: Paul sends Onesimus back to his master Philemon — not as a mere slave now, but as a beloved brother.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their _____.
verse: And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness.
note: Ezekiel's hearers enjoyed him like a lovely song (33:32) — but their hearts went after 'covetousness.' Hearers, not doers.
